What to record: Identify the released project, material batch, and cut-list revision.
Record who set up and ran the process plus the production date.
Identify machine, blade, bit, cutter, jig, or program version.
State the face, edge, fence, stop, datum, or coordinate origin.

What to record: Record actual thickness, part ID, fit class, and finish allowance.
Record cutter, target width, depth, shoulder, and offset.
Record face, edge, fence side, pass count, and order relative to sizing.
Example: Inside face down / groove before crosscut

What to record: Record measured joint, sample fit, first part, and interval checks.
